clue.text: Cheap device for identifying church by stream

parts.note: a PIN is a personal identification number, used to identify you at a cash machine
a beck is a northern English word for a stream

explanation.surface: Someone describes a cheap gadget for spotting a church beside a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinchbeck was a copper-zinc alloy made to look like gold, hence the adjective for anything showy but cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means sham or tawdry, from the imitation-gold alloy named after its inventor.

clue.text: Crossing street, fork out for meat and veg pie

indicators.note: crossing means the outer word straddles the street's letters

parts.note: to fork out is to pay

explanation.surface: Someone crosses the road to pay for a savoury pie.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasty is a folded pastry case filled with meat and vegetables, as in the Cornish variety.

clue.text: Takeover involving island girl taking time in race

indicators.note: in means the island, girl and time all go inside the race

parts.note: a nation is a people or race

indicators.note: taking means the girl acquires the next letter, placed after her

parts.note: Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides
Lisa is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A takeover sees an island girl clocking a time in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Nationalisation is the state's takeover of a private industry into public ownership.

clue.text: Problem identified by top teacher, a revolutionary

parts.note: the head is the head teacher of a school
Che Guevara was the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: A head teacher spots a trouble-making radical in school.
explanation.definitionFit: A headache, figuratively, is a troublesome problem or worry.

clue.text: Some of them irritated a Muslim ruler

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people were annoyed by an Islamic potentate.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a title for a ruler or commander in Muslim countries.

clue.text: Flyer's angle accepted by two monarchs

indicators.note: accepted by means the angling word is taken in between the two monarchs

parts.note: a king and ER, the abbreviation for Elizabeth Regina
to angle is to fish

explanation.surface: A pilot's viewpoint is endorsed by two kings.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingfisher is a brightly coloured bird, and a bird is something that flies.

clue.text: Ring included in goods left by old Russian writer

indicators.note: included in means the ring's letter goes inside the two Gs

parts.note: G is short for good, so goods are two Gs
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A ring tucked among goods that an old Russian author left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Nikolai Gogol wrote Dead Souls and The Government Inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: Gogol is a famous nineteenth-century Russian novelist and dramatist, so he is an example of the category.

clue.text: Game birds finally heading for one of several rivers

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of each of the words heading and for

parts.note: there are several English rivers called the Ouse

explanation.surface: Game birds at last flying off towards one of many rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Grouse are plump birds shot for sport on moors, classic game birds; the plural is the same word.

clue.text: Regiment's drug raid sergeant mostly organised

indicators.note: organised means these letters are arranged into a new order
mostly means the word sergeant loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A regimental sergeant largely set up a drugs raid.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grenadier Guards are a senior infantry regiment of the British Army's Household Division.

clue.text: Licensed church member, top person around Scottish port

indicators.note: around means the leader's letters surround the port

parts.note: a leader is the person at the top
Ayr is a port on the west coast of Scotland

explanation.surface: A church official is the boss around a Scottish harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay reader is a layperson licensed by a bishop to lead services and preach.

clue.text: Arrive with post, ultimately attracted by TV serial

parts.note: a post is a job or position, a situation
to arrive is to come

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of each of the words attracted and by

explanation.surface: Someone arrives with the post and is drawn in by a television series.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitcom is a broadcast comedy series with recurring characters, which loosely counts as a television serial.

clue.text: One-time royal attendant in the old country

parts.note: ye is an old form of the, as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe
Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A former servant of the crown living in some old land.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeomen of the Guard were historically royal bodyguards and attendants to the English monarch.

clue.text: One's first step, embracing females in the wings

indicators.note: embracing means the outer letters hug the females' letters
first means take only the opening letter of the word One's

parts.note: a stage is a step in a process
F is the abbreviation for female, so two Fs are females

explanation.surface: A dancer's first step involves holding women while waiting in the wings.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor waiting in the wings is out of the audience's view, beside the stage rather than on it.

clue.text: Cricketer is mad at first about duke's censorship

indicators.note: about means the cricketer's letters go around the duke

parts.note: a bowler is a cricketer who delivers the ball
D is the abbreviation for duke

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of the word mad

explanation.surface: A cricketer is angry about a nobleman's cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Bowdler produced an expurgated Shakespeare, so bowdlerism is prudish censorship.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowdlerism is the removal of supposedly offensive passages from a text, a form of censorship.

clue.text: Instruct theatre audience: there may be a gig here

definitions.text: there may be a gig here

parts.note: to coach is to instruct or train
the house is the audience in a theatre, as in a full house

explanation.surface: A director tells a theatre audience that a concert may be staged there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gig' suggests a concert, but here it is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach house is an outbuilding where carriages such as a gig were kept.

clue.text: Officer allowed to entertain one associated with place of study

parts.note: COL is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the outer letters hold one inside

parts.note: legal means allowed by law
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An officer is permitted to host someone linked to a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Collegial means relating to a college, which is an institution for study.

clue.text: Heartless devil's discovery

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a fiend is a devil

explanation.surface: A cruel devil makes a discovery.
explanation.definitionFit: A find is something discovered, often a valuable or lucky one.

clue.text: As letters may be, initially encouraging headlong rush

parts.note: letters for posting may be stamped

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of encouraging

explanation.surface: Mail, stamped at first, sparks an encouraging dash.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden panicked rush of a herd or crowd.

clue.text: Atmosphere associated with large animal's retreat

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes
an air is an atmosphere or feeling about a place

explanation.surface: A mood that comes with a big beast's hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is the den where a wild animal rests and hides.

clue.text: Enterprising type coming right across river

indicators.note: across means the first pieces stretch over the river, holding it within

parts.note: an advent is a coming or arrival
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A bold person arrives and heads straight over the river.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventurer is someone who seeks risky new undertakings, a person of enterprise.

clue.text: Silver, say, provided by Irish tucking into hors d'oeuvre

indicators.note: tucking into means the Irish letters are put inside the starter

parts.note: pâté is a spread often served as a starter

explanation.surface: Silver, perhaps, is provided by an Irishman eating his starter.
explanation.walkthrough: Silver is Long John Silver, the pirate in Stevenson's Treasure Island, not the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Long John Silver is the best-known fictional buccaneer, so he is an example.

clue.text: Candidate's former partner meeting friend born in Paris

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
ami is French for friend; the clue's in Paris applies to it too
née is French for born, used of a woman's maiden name

explanation.surface: An exam candidate's ex meets a friend who was born in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: An examinee is someone sitting a test, a candidate in an examination.

clue.text: Coarse little devil about to pinch uniform

indicators.note: to pinch means to squeeze something tightly in, so the uniform letter goes inside

parts.note: an imp is a small devil
re means about or concerning
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A rude little devil is about to steal a uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Impure can mean coarse or unrefined, mixed with baser matter.

clue.text: English head going over German city

indicators.note: going over means the word for head is turned back to front in this down clue

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness

explanation.surface: An English boss travels across to a city in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is a large industrial city in the Ruhr region of western Germany.

clue.text: Woman from north involved in Muslim festival

indicators.note: involved in means the north letter is wrapped inside the festival

parts.note: Eid is a Muslim festival, such as Eid al-Fitr

explanation.surface: A northern woman takes part in a Muslim celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a female given name, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: Form of flattery originally praising peer's jewellery

parts.note: imitation is said to be the sincerest form of flattery

indicators.note: originally means the opening letter of praising

parts.note: an earl is a peer, and earl's reads as EARLS

explanation.surface: Copying a nobleman, while praising him, extends to his jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: Imitation pearls are fake gems strung as a necklace, a kind of costume jewellery.

clue.text: Breather required before everyone's third jab

parts.note: a lung is what you breathe with

indicators.note: third picks the third letter of the word everyone's

explanation.surface: A rest is needed before everyone gets their third vaccine jab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breather' looks like a pause and 'jab' like an injection; one is an organ and the other a fencing thrust.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a sudden thrust forward, as in fencing, much like a jab.

clue.text: New sidesman receiving nothing in July, perhaps

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A new church sidesman takes in no collection in July.
explanation.walkthrough: A sidesman is a church usher who takes the collection.
explanation.definitionFit: July falls in the middle of the summer season, so it is an example of a midseason time.
